concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: The original breach notification clause requires notice within 48 hours, and the amendment changing this to 24 hours only takes effect on 1 October 2026, after 15 September 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1 replaces the 48-hour limit with 24 hours, effective 1 October 2026, so it is in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1 reduces the on-site audit notice period from 30 days to 20 days, effective 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The replacement liability clause in Amendment No. 1, effective 1 October 2026, sets a fixed aggregate cap of EUR 1,000,000 for Processor breaches, independent of fees paid.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The replacement liability clause in Amendment No. 1 states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality section.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed as an approved Sub-processor in the original DPA's annex, and its withdrawal only takes effect on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: Amendment No. 1 withdraws approval of Meridian Mail Ltd with effect from 1 January 2027, and no later approval is recorded.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, personal data is stored or processed in Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, France and Denmark, with Ireland no longer authorised after the 1 January 2027 withdrawal.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: Amendment No. 1 replaces the 90-day deletion period with 60 days, which runs from termination on 31 December 2026 to 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting personal data it processes under the dpa.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting personal data it processes under the DPA.
justifications: This summary reflects the 24-hour outer limit that replaced the earlier 48-hour period from 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: Usable privileged credential exposure was confirmed on 10 April, which triggers the 12-hour expedited outer limit measured from the original awareness. The expedited limit applies even though the credential exposure was confirmed later.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April, so the 12-hour expedited outer limit expired at 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice was delivered at 06:00 that day, 50 minutes after the limit.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The follow-up report is due by the end of the third Business Day after awareness on Friday 9 April. Business days 12 April (closure) and 14 April (approved pause) are excluded, so the count runs 13, 15 and 16 April.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: Hold H-23 is the last hold to end on 25 August 2027, so the 60-day ordinary deadline (29 August) is overtaken by the tenth Business Day after release, which is 9 September 2027. The contractual closure of 30 August is excluded from the count.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: Backup BK-0630 was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records, so it must be deleted by the earlier of its ordinary deadline and 35 calendar days after creation. The restoration on 20 July does not restart this period.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: On 1 September 2027 the holds have ended and the ordinary deadline has passed, so the records remain only under the hold-based deletion window. Records retained solely under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation, excluding service delivery and analytics.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval for the Stockholm infrastructure service begins no earlier than the latest of the proposed start date, the completed security review, and written consent. The security review completed on 22 April 2027, which is later than the 20 April start date and the 18 April consent.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Added as an approved Sub-processor for transactional email delivery from 1 January 2027 and continuing ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd's withdrawal is not reversed for ordinary customer email by the emergency permission.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: These countries have actual processing (storage in Norway and Estonia, monitoring in Lithuania, email in France, Stockholm infrastructure in Sweden) and effective approval as of 15 May 2027. Ireland is excluded because the emergency permission expired on 11 May 2027, and Denmark is excluded because its authorisation was withdrawn on 10 May 2027.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: The security cap is the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice Qualifying Fees, which total EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT, the service credit, training and the event month's prepaid fees. Twice that amount, EUR 2,280,000, exceeds EUR 2,000,000.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap of EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year is reduced by the EUR 300,000 in ordinary payments already made in the current Contract Year, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Ordinary claim C-1 is limited to the EUR 700,000 remaining ordinary pool, security loss L-2 is fully payable within the remaining EUR 1,780,000 security pool, and confidentiality claims C-4 and C-5 are uncapped at EUR 350,000. The total is EUR 2,800,000.
